content:
incident-bot: Paging on-call: automated regression detector flagged a model/quantization quality drop for tenant AcmeCorp (tenant_id=acme-42) in dedicated pool eu-west-1-dedicated-3. Correlated with recent quant profile rollout 'q4_8_v2' at 2026-03-15T08:12Z. Severity: P2. Potential customer-impact: increased hallucinations and ~12% drop on rerank F1 for production eval set. Please ack and triage.
jon_oncall: Acked. I'm on it, paging SRE + ML. @alex_sre @sara_ml can you take a look? I'll start a command line trace on the pool.
alex_sre: Looking at serving logs now — I see a spike in token latencies for acme-42 around the rollout time and a bunch of quantization warnings: "scale out-of-range" + repeated fallback to slower kernels. Pulling worker logs.
sara_ml: Confirmed — we deployed a tenant-specific quant profile tweak (q4_8_v2) as part of an optimization experiment at 08:12 UTC. That profile was only targeted to acme-42 for cost/perf testing. Rolling back ASAP is my recommendation if quality regressions are customer-visible.
emily_re: Can we isolate tenant routing to a safe baseline model before rollback? If routing change is fast we can avoid redeploys.
liu_ops: We can flip a router override for tenant to route to model variant redwood-1.3-fp16 (baseline) in the control plane. Doing a dry-run check of compat flags.
kate_support: Looping in account manager and CS: @mike_am @kate_support -> Mike, Amy: heads-up for customer comms. Need to confirm impact window and ETA to mitigation.
mike_am: Thanks. I will message the customer with a brief (no blame): "We detected an internal inference tuning that impacted your model quality; we're rolling you back to the previous profile now and expect resolution within 10-15 minutes. We'll follow up with details and a postmortem." OK?
jon_oncall: Good. Alex/Sara, what's the rollback command or mitigation plan? Prefer no disruptive full redeploy.
sara_ml: Plan:
1) Router override -> route acme-42 -> redwood-1.3-fp16 (baseline) to stop using q4_8_v2 immediately.
2) Revert quant profile for tenant in config store from q4_8_v2 -> q4_8_v1 (previous stable) — can be done via platform API.
3) Monitor quality metrics and logs for 30m, then remove override if stable.
Commands I'll run in order:
```
# create router override
redwoodctl routing set-override --tenant acme-42 --model redwood-1.3-fp16 --reason "rollback q4_8_v2 regression"
# rollback quant profile
redwoodctl tenant config update --tenant acme-42 --set "quant_profile=q4_8_v1"
# verify
redwoodctl tenant status --tenant acme-42 --fields model,quant_profile,active_workers
```
alex_sre: I'll prepare a fallback at infra level in case kernels keep falling back — set worker memory limits and restart loop for only acme-42 workers if necessary. Trying router override now.
deploy-bot: Router override requested: id=ovr-20260315-01, target=redwood-1.3-fp16, tenant=acme-42. Estimated propagation 20s.
deploy-bot: Router override applied successfully to eu-west-1-dedicated-3 for tenant acme-42.
liu_ops: Override observed in routing table. Traffic for acme-42 now hitting redwood-1.3-fp16. Beginning traffic shadowing checks.
alex_sre: Early metrics (first 2 min): latency stable, no kernel fallback warnings for acme-42. Good sign.
sara_ml: Rolling quant profile back in config store now.
deploy-bot: Tenant config update accepted: acme-42.quant_profile=q4_8_v1 (was q4_8_v2). Change-id=cfg-8942. No restart required.
jon_oncall: Nice. Can we run a quick sample eval (10 queries) against prod traffic sample to validate quality? Sara/Emily please run.
emily_re: Running 10-prod-sample eval against baseline model variant + saved prompts from acme-42. Results: mean F1 back to baseline within noise (+/-1%). Spot checks look OK.
sara_ml: I'll keep the router override in place for 30m and then remove once metrics pass: rollout monitor -> quality_alert threshold set to 5% drop.
alex_sre: Worker logs cleared from the earlier warnings. Looks like the q4_8_v2 path triggered a quantization mismatch on some attention kernels under this tenant's token distribution.
kate_support: Mike/CS, I've sent the customer notification: "Mitigation applied; we rolled back your internal tuning and restored the prior model profile. We'll follow up with the root cause and timeline. Please reply if you still see issues." Customer replied: "Thanks, will watch performance and alert us if anything odd." Good.
mike_am: I'll schedule a follow-up call tomorrow to walk through details with the customer. Thanks team.
jon_oncall: Moving to monitoring mode. On-call handoff note: daytime oncall @alex_day will take over at 09:00 UTC — leaving a handoff msg in #oncall-handoffs with current state (override in place, config reverted, metrics nominal). Postmortem owner: sara_ml. Action items: 1) add canary checks for tenant-specific quant rollouts, 2) make tenant-targeted rollout ramp slower and require manual ack for quality regressions, 3) add automated rollback policy for >5% quality drop.
sara_ml: I'll own the postmortem and start drafting. Will include instrumentation gaps and a proposed change to the rollout UI to flag per-tenant quality signals before enabling.
jon_oncall: Thanks everyone. I'll keep incident open till 09:30 UTC for final verification, then close. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation applied at 2026-03-15T08:27Z (router override + config revert). Customer impact window ~08:12-08:27 UTC. P2 -> monitoring. Owner=sara_ml."
